'''Michael Ernest O'Nan''' (August 9, 1943, [[Fort Knox, Kentucky]] – July 31, 2017, [[Princeton, New Jersey]])<ref>{{cite web|url=https://matherhodge.com/tribute/details/1112/Michael-O-Nan/obituary.html |title=Obituary of Michael E O'Nan}}</ref> was an American mathematician, specializing in group theory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.centraljersey.com/obituaries/michael-e-o-nan-phd/article_9f95dd0e-76cf-11e7-9b65-3376f24c64df.html|title=Michael E. O'Nan, PhD, 73|website=centraljersey.com|access-date=August 2, 2017}}</ref>

O'Nan received his PhD in 1970 from [[Princeton University]] under [[Daniel Gorenstein]] with thesis ''A Characterization of the Three-Dimensional Projective Unitary Group over a Finite Field''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=5935}}</ref> He was a professor at [[Rutgers University]]. In 1976 he found strong evidence for the existence of a [[sporadic group]],<ref>{{cite journal|author=Michael E. O'Nan|title=Some evidence for the existence of a new simple group|journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society|series=3rd Series|volume=32|issue=3|year=1976|issn=0024-6115|pages=421–79|doi=10.1112/plms/s3-32.3.421}}</ref> which [[Charles Sims (mathematician)|Charles Sims]] constructed. The group is commonly called the [[O'Nan group]] after O'Nan.<ref>{{Cite journal | mode = cs2| title = A new construction of the O'Nan simple group | last = Ryba | first = A. J. E. | journal = [[Journal of Algebra]] | year = 1988 | volume = 112 | number = 1 | pages = 173–197 | mr = 0921973}}</ref>

The [[O'Nan–Scott theorem]] in group theory is also named after O'Nan, who discovered it independently from Leonard Scott. It describes the [[maximal subgroup]]s of the [[symmetric group]]s.{{citation needed|date=December 2017}}
